governance.note: Continuation of the pjm-52 coal-bit sticky-stack base (pjm-48 coal keeper + pjm-49 MISO/NYISO realized-LMP heat-rate anchors + pjm-50 firm-export floor / losses hurdle / TVA-LGEE seams + pjm-51 Southeast gas-INELASTIC affine reference price + the MISO coal-bituminous 3-lever stack), all previously attested. NEW this run: ONE structural lever, pjm_zonal_gas_basis. It shifts each PJM gas unit by its zone's MEASURED delivered-to-electric-power gas basis vs Henry Hub (EIA series N3045<ST>3M by the zone's primary state -- IL/OH/OH/WV/PA/VA/NJ/MD for ComEd/AEP_Ohio/ATSI/West_APS/Central_PA/Dominion/EMAAC/SWMAAC; data/raw/pjm_zonal_gas_hub.csv), a forward-reproducible measured power-plant delivered cost that regenerates every year from forward state-level EIA gas data and responds to changed regional supply (rule #12). The per-zone basis is anchored to a gas-CAPACITY-weighted mean of ZERO so the calibrated PJM fleet-aggregate gas level (the gas_monthly_actuals ISO-month series) is byte-preserved and ONLY the cross-zonal spread opens; the coal-sigmoid reference stays on the ISO mean (no level shift). WV 2025 (11/12 months EIA-withheld -- only January, a winter spike) is proxied to the OH+PA Appalachian delivered-to-EP mean, documented in the CSV source column; not residual-tuned. No residual-tuned adders, no load proxy, no haircut, no output pinning to actuals -- the basis enters as a measured physical fuel-cost input, never as the answer. RESULT: the lever is structurally correct but INERT. The zonal LMP spread is exactly $0.00 in all 8760 hours of all three years (perfect copper-plate, unchanged from pjm-52), and the dispatch is within noise (2024 COAL_BIT 97.2 vs 96.6, net export +61.0 vs +63.0). DIAGNOSIS: the PJM copper-plate is a reduced-NETWORK artifact, not a gas-pricing one -- the priced PJM_external node is a single price hub wired to 5 of 8 zones with ~30 GW of uncongested transfer (4.9-7.5 GW each) and the internal TTCs (3-8 GW) are loose relative to flows, so even a real $0.47-0.87/MMBtu dear-east/cheap-west gas spread (~$3-6/MWh at the burner tip) makes NO internal link bind: cheap western supply floods east and to the export hub unconstrained and ties every zone's energy-balance dual to one price. The lever is measured, flow-blind, forward-reproducible market structure and is correct to keep once the network congests (rule #1), but it is NOT the lever for the binding constraint. C6 PASS (measured input, no residual fit, exogenous historic outages). NOT a keeper; pjm-48 remains the PJM keeper. Next lever must tighten the PJM TTCs / rework the external star node so the network actually congests before zonal gas pricing can separate the LMP.
